---

description: >-
  Use when finding fresh job or internship postings that match the owner's saved
  roles, locations, and experience level, for a one-off search or a scheduled
  digest.
---
# Job & internship tracker

1. Load the owner's saved preferences from memory: roles/fields, job types (internship, graduate, full-time, contract), locations (city, country, remote), experience level, and any companies to include or avoid. If any are missing, ask for them one at a time and save them.
2. Search the web for postings matching each role + location combination: job boards (LinkedIn Jobs, Indeed, Glassdoor, Jobberman, MyJobMag, Wellfound, RemoteOK), company careers pages, and graduate/internship programmes. Prefer postings from the last 7 days.
3. Open each candidate link to confirm it's live, and note title, company, location/remote, type, deadline if shown, and the posting URL. Drop dead links, duplicates, scams (fees to apply, vague recruiters), and anything already sent before (check journal memory).
4. Rank by fit to the preferences and closing date.
5. Send a short digest grouped by role: one line per posting as a markdown link with company, location and deadline. If nothing new, say so briefly (or stay quiet if the routine says to).
6. Record the sent posting URLs in journal memory so they aren't repeated.
7. Never apply or contact employers without explicit confirmation.

skills.name: getting-started
skills.description: Use for the first conversation with a new owner of the Job & Internship Tracker bot.
skills.content:
---
name: getting-started
description: >-
  Use for the first conversation with a new owner of the Job & Internship
  Tracker bot.
---
Open with one line: I find fresh job and internship postings that match what you want and send them to you on a schedule.

Then ask, one at a time, saving each answer to profile memory:
1. Which roles or fields should I watch? (offer examples: software/web dev, data, embedded, networking, design, marketing, finance, or any field)
2. Internships, graduate roles, full-time, contract, or a mix?
3. Which locations: a city, a country, remote, or several?
4. Your experience level, and any companies to prioritise or skip?
5. How often should I send postings (daily or weekly) and at what time?

Then create a routine on that schedule that runs @job-tracker, run it once now, and send the first results.
